repositories.name: platform-contracts
repositories.reason: Source of truth for the schemas and OpenAPI specs that change: add optional column tags to ingestion.schema.discovered.v1, add column classification fields to metadata.dataset.changed.v1 and the metadata-graph Column schema, add a new classification endpoint, add masked_columns to the entitlements Decision and the query response; ship as minor release 2.4.0.

repositories.name: platform-sdk
repositories.reason: SDK models are explicit dataclasses that drop undeclared fields, so Column needs classification/tags, Decision needs masked_columns, MetadataClient needs a set-classification method, and the bundled platform-contracts pin must move to 2.4.0 (release 3.5.0); otherwise every SDK consumer silently loses the new fields.

repositories.name: metadata-graph
repositories.reason: Owning service: store classification per column node, suggest it from ingested source tags without overwriting steward overrides on re-discovery, add the steward set/override endpoint, and return classification from GET columns and in metadata.dataset.changed.v1.

repositories.name: ingestion-service
repositories.reason: The Postgres connector already reads the column comment holding source tags (e.g. 'tags: pii,email') but drops it, so it must parse the tags and publish them on ingestion.schema.discovered.v1.

repositories.name: entitlements-service
repositories.reason: Access decisions must list the PII-classified columns to mask when the principal lacks a pii:read grant, which requires fetching column classifications from metadata-graph, caching and invalidating them on metadata.dataset.changed.v1, and adding masked_columns to the Decision.

repositories.name: query-gateway
repositories.reason: Enforcement happens in the caller, so the gateway must mask the columns named in decision.masked_columns in returned rows (and report which columns were masked) before responding to data consumers.

repositories.name: dq-engine
repositories.reason: Rules are selected only by data_type today, so dq-engine needs PII-format validation rules and a classification-based binding that applies them to columns classified PII (read via MetadataClient.get_columns on SDK 3.5.0).

repositories.name: search-indexer
repositories.reason: It validates metadata.dataset.changed.v1 against a stale vendored schema (platform-contracts 2.1.0) with additionalProperties:false on columns, so any new column field would send every event to search-indexer.dlq; the vendored schema must be updated and deployed before metadata-graph emits the new fields.

repositories.name: platform-e2e
repositories.reason: Cross-service changes require new or updated suites here: tags-to-classification ingestion, steward override, masked query results with and without pii:read, and PII DQ rules.

repositories.name: reporting-service
repositories.reason: Listed in the metadata-graph README as a consumer of metadata.dataset.changed.v1 but not in this workspace, so its reader tolerance for the new column fields is unknown and must be verified by its owners before metadata-graph emits them.

considered_not_impacted.name: lineage-service
considered_not_impacted.reason: Consumes metadata.dataset.changed.v1 but reads only dataset.urn and dataset.name as a tolerant reader, and SDK subscribe does not validate payloads, so additive column fields do not affect it.

considered_not_impacted.name: notification-service
considered_not_impacted.reason: Consumes only dataset_urn and score from dq.result.published.v1 and owner from get_dataset, none of which change shape; new PII rules may lower scores and raise alert volume (tracked as a risk, not a code change).

considered_not_impacted.name: usage-metering
considered_not_impacted.reason: Consumes gateway.access.logged.v1, which this plan leaves unchanged (principal, dataset_urn, row_count).

contracts.name: ingestion.schema.discovered.v1
contracts.description: Add optional columns[].tags (array of lowercase strings parsed from the source column comment, e.g. ["pii","email"]); schema lives in platform-contracts 2.4.0.

contracts.name: metadata.dataset.changed.v1
contracts.description: Add optional dataset.columns[].classification (enum PUBLIC|INTERNAL|CONFIDENTIAL|PII, nullable), columns[].classification_source (SUGGESTED|STEWARD) and columns[].tags; change_type enum unchanged (classification edits emit UPDATED). Additive per platform-contracts rules, but breaking for search-indexer's strict vendored schema until it is updated.

contracts.name: GET /v1/datasets/{urn}/columns
contracts.description: Column schema gains optional classification, classification_source and tags fields (metadata-graph API 1.5.0).

contracts.name: PUT /v1/datasets/{urn}/columns/{column_name}/classification
contracts.description: Steward sets or overrides a column classification (body {classification}); stores it with classification_source=STEWARD, returns the column, publishes metadata.dataset.changed.v1 (UPDATED); 400 on invalid value, 404 on unknown dataset/column, 403 if caller is not a steward.

contracts.name: POST /v1/access/decide
contracts.description: Decision response gains masked_columns (array of column names, default []) listing PII-classified columns when the principal lacks pii:read; allow/reason/policy_id unchanged (entitlements API 1.3.0).

contracts.name: POST /v1/query
contracts.description: 200 response gains optional masked_columns (array of column names); values of those columns in rows are replaced with a mask value for principals without pii:read (row shape and keys unchanged; query API 2.1.0).

open_questions: Tag-to-classification mapping: is it 'pii' tag -> PII only, and which tags (if any) map to CONFIDENTIAL/INTERNAL/PUBLIC? What is the default for untagged columns (null/unclassified assumed, which is not masked)?
Should the mapping from tags to a suggested classification live in metadata-graph (assumed, so policy stays with the owning team) or in ingestion-service (emitting suggested_classification)?
Scope of the pii:read grant: global 'pii:read' (assumed) or scoped like 'domain:<domain>:pii:read' / 'dataset:<urn>:pii:read'? Who administers it?
Should CONFIDENTIAL columns also be masked or restricted, or only PII as the ticket states?
Mask representation in query results: fixed string (e.g. '***') for string columns and null for others (assumed), hashing, or partial masking? Typed BI consumers may break on type changes.

How does query-gateway map arbitrary SQL output columns (aliases, expressions, joins across datasets) back to source columns? Name-based masking on the single dataset_urn is leaky; is SQL parsing/rewriting or warehouse-side masking required?
Who is a steward and how is the PUT classification endpoint authorized (no auth is visible in metadata-graph today)?
Should PII-format rule selection use the source tag subtype (email, phone, ssn) stored on the column (assumed) or explicit rule bindings via dq-engine POST /v1/rules?
Should new PII rules count toward the dataset DQ score immediately (could trigger more notification-service alerts) or run report-only first?
reporting-service is not in this workspace: is it a tolerant reader of metadata.dataset.changed.v1, and does it display or export column data that must also be masked?
Are there other query/export paths to data besides query-gateway (e.g. reporting-service, direct warehouse access) that also need masking?
Should gateway.access.logged.v1 record masked_columns for audit? Not included in this plan to keep usage-metering untouched.
Backfill: should existing datasets be re-discovered to populate suggested classifications, and should stewards review before masking is enforced?
The int_env fixture used by platform-e2e is not in the workspace; where are its helpers (grant, ingest_table, query) defined and who extends them?
